name: Nǁng

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Nǁng (nngg1234).

notes: Tuu (!Ui branch) click language of South Africa (Nǁng/Nǀuu), critically endangered. This is an honest PARTIAL skeleton: there is no single standardized community orthography, and the descriptive literature presents the inventory in phonetic transcription rather than a settled spelling. The five click places and the g-/n-/h-/x-/glottal accompaniment digraphs above follow general Khoisanist transcription convention and are plausible but not confirmed as official. Tone and many finer click airstream and phonation contrasts are still not represented, so a substantial PER floor is expected. Nǁng/Nǀuu tone is not consistently recoverable from the partial community orthography and is left unencoded; stress is not a separate contrastive category (documented exemption). Tier stays at skeleton (not research) despite the cited Namaseb 2022 dictionary/sketch: the grapheme table itself remains an unconfirmed plausible transcription convention, not the settled community spelling the research tier presumes. Added coverage: plain t/c/j/f and the ty/tyh/dy/ky digraphs for the pre-palatal stop series and Afrikaans/English loan consonants; â/ê/î/ô/û as the alternate circumflex nasalization diacritic seen alongside the tilde series in community-dictionary transcriptions; <q>/<qh> after a click letter for the linguo-pulmonic contour click series (click + delayed uvular release, per Miller et al.'s reanalysis cited on the Nǁng Wikipedia page); <q> after an oral or (circumflex-marked) nasal vowel for pharyngealization (aq/eq/iq/oq/uq and âq/êq/îq/ôq/ûq -> Vˤ/Ṽˤ); <ʻ> for the glottal stop, including as an alternate glottalized-click spelling next to the existing apostrophe series; and a bare <ʼ> ejective diacritic for pulmonic obstruents outside the click system (kxʼ, tsʼ), which also composes with the existing click+x digraphs to cover the linguo-glottalic affricate series (ǀxʼ, ǃxʼ, ǁxʼ, ǂxʼ) without a new table entry. Left unresolved (documented, not guessed at): a handful of gold tokens where <q> occurs with neither a preceding vowel nor a preceding click (kqoqo, kqâi), and one isolated ds-cluster (dsyhîn) whose 'd' does not fit the dy=ɟ pattern. Individual Nǀuu entries on Wiktionary (citing the Namaseb-led 2022 Nǀuuki dictionary) were checked as attested forms, not cited as a source, for the four grapheme patterns absent from the skeleton table: circumflex vowels as an alternate nasalization diacritic (kôea /kõeə/, tsâa /tsɑ̃ɑ̃/, nǁâi /ᵑǁə̃ĩ/), <q> after a vowel marking pharyngealization (ǀhaqoka /ǀʰəoˤokə/), <q>/<qh> after a click letter for the linguo-pulmonic contour click series (ǁqhuu /ǁqʰuu/), and <ʻ>/<ʼ> as glottal-stop and ejective diacritics respectively (haqaʻi /hɑˤɑʔi/, kxʼaa /kχʼɑɑ/).
